subject: how a person decides which clinic or hospital to use, and when they go past the nearest one
citation: Majola TN et al. (2026). Healthcare workers' perspectives on patient bypassing of Primary Health Care facilities in Mpumalanga province, South Africa. African Journal of Primary Health Care & Family Medicine. doi:10.4102/phcfm.v18i1.5368
Chavalala L et al. (2025). General Male Patients' Experiences When Visiting Public Health Facilities in Limpopo Province, South Africa. Public Health Challenges. doi:10.1002/puh2.70166

claims.text: Unfamiliarity with the referral system makes clinic-first entry read as optional, because patients do not know the correct starting point and go straight to casualty or hospital.
Negative experience of clinics as slow, under-resourced, and staffed by rude workers makes clinic-first rules read as burdensome, because patients judge the clinic as not worth following.
evaluative_rules: Judge a facility by whether it wastes your time, not by the official pathway.
Judge a facility by whether staff treat you like a human being.
objections: Will this waste my time like the clinic does?
Will the staff treat me like a human being?

claims.text: Local clinics staffed by known community members with shared consulting rooms make locally delivered care read as exposing, because patients fear stigma and loss of confidentiality.
evaluative_rules: Judge a facility by whether your neighbours can see or learn your condition.
objections: Will people in my community see me or learn my condition?

claims.text: Public facilities read as unwelcoming and unsafe for men, because male patients experience long waits, gender-biased triage, and humiliating treatment by female nurses.
evaluative_rules: Judge a facility by whether it welcomes men rather than prioritising women.

claims.text: Clinic-based nurse interaction reads as threatening, because patients expect mistreatment from nurses based on experienced or reported harsh and disrespectful behaviour.
evaluative_rules: Judge a facility by whether nurses will keep your condition private and speak to you respectfully.
objections: Will I be humiliated or shouted at by nurses?

region: Mpumalanga and Limpopo provinces, South Africa
confidence: Two qualitative studies: 20 healthcare workers at 10 Mpumalanga hospitals (so the bypassing reasons are staff-reported, not patients' own words) and 28 men in four focus groups in Limpopo. Fieldwork dates are not stated in either paper; the years shown are publication years. Mechanisms durable; magnitudes unknown.
